To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a semiautomated pipeline can be used to reliably track the evolution of enhancing lesions to BHs in MS and that this pipeline is applicable to a large cohort of MS patients and to different clinical trial designs and settings.

we developed a semiautomated pipeline that tracks gadolinium‐ enhancing multiple sclerosis (MS ) lesions and converts them into T1 hypointense persistent black holes (BHs) and that this pipeline is validated by a manual tracking approach in a clinical trial.
a semiautomated pipeline for the tracking of enhancing multiple sclerosis lesions to persistent T1‐hypoinetense black holes can be used to evaluate tissue loss and repair in clinical trials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a semiautomated pipeline for tracking enhancing lesions to persistent T1 BHs.
the development and validation of a semiautomated method for the detection and tracking of enhancing and persistent BHs in MS patients.
developing and testing a new method to identify persistent BHs in MS patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study are promising and suggest that the proposed pipeline is able to track the evolution of enhancing lesions in MS patients with a good level of agreement.
the results from the present study do not support the hypothesis that the presence of persistent black holes is associated with a worse outcome in multiple sclerosis.
the use of a semiautomated pipeline for tracking enhancing lesions to BHs is a valid approach for large‐scale trials and could provide a useful tool for the assessment of tissue repair in MS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to develop an algorithm to track the evolution of MS lesions and that this algorithm is robust, reliable, and reproducible.
we have validated a semiautomated pipeline for tracking the evolution of enhancing lesions to BHs and that this pipeline is robust and reliable.
we have shown a way to track the evolution of gadolinium‐positive multiple sclerosis lesions to persistent T1 black holes in a semi-automated manner, and that the method is valid and reliable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tracking of individual gadolinium‐ enhancing lesions to BHs in MS can be performed with a semiautomated pipeline in a reasonable time and with a high level of accuracy and reproducibility.
we can track the evolution of individual enhancing lesions to persistent T1 hypointense lesions using a semiautomated segmentation approach.
a semiautomated pipeline for the individual tracking of MS lesions is feasible, and that this approach can be applied to large datasets.
